headline: Council enrolled inclusionary zoning changes with new incentives and granted National Grid poles on Blane Street and nearby streets.
summary: The council enrolled changes to inclusionary zoning, lowering the affordable unit requirement from 15% to 10% and adding incentives for developers. It granted National Grid pole and conduit petitions at four locations, with conditions, and split off a Broadway and Eastern Avenue item to come back as a new petition. It referred a six-story hotel height proposal and an $800,000 Public Works budget change to committee.
decisions: Approved the reappointments of Dr. Scoon Carrington, John Colangeli, and Dr. Qunao Singh to the Board of Health, unanimously.
Split the Broadway and Eastern Avenue underground conduit item from the National Grid petition, with the petitioner to file a new petition.
Granted National Grid's pole and conduit petitions at four locations, with conditions, including moving the new pole at 6 Blane Street to 30 feet south of pole 2023.
Referred to the Rules and Ordinance Committee a proposal to set the maximum height for motels and hotels at six stories, not to exceed 75 feet.
Enrolled the change moving supervision of the animal control officer from the Police Department to the Health Department, 9 to 0 with one member present.
Referred to the Finance Committee an order cutting $800,000 from the FY 2027 Public Works budget for the FY 2026 snow and ice deficit.
Approved, unanimously, an ordinance changing the zoning use table to allow more business uses by right in several business, highway, commercial, and industrial zones.
Approved, unanimously, an ordinance adding a salary schedule for assistant department heads.
Approved amendments to the inclusionary zoning paper changing the definition of an inclusionary project and removing the mixed-income definition, 9 to 1.
Failed: an amendment to keep the 15% affordable housing requirement in the inclusionary zoning ordinance.
Chair ruled that the inclusionary zoning paper would not be split.
Enrolled the inclusionary zoning ordinance update, which reduces the affordable unit requirement from 15% to 10%, 9 to 1.
Enrolled the inclusionary zoning incentives as amended, including height bonuses outside Residence A districts and new parking ratios, 9 to 0.
Adopted a transfer of $157,000 from Salary Reserve to assistant department director salaries across several departments, 9 to 0.
Adopted a transfer of $220,000 from Salary Reserve to Police Salaries, 9 to 0.
discussion: Inclusionary zoning affordable share: Members said the 15% requirement was hard to meet given current costs and interest rates, while others said the percentage was not the main barrier and pointed to moratoriums, height limits, and parking rules.

Parking rules: Members discussed 1.1 parking spaces per market unit and 0.7 per affordable unit, and said parking requirements raise costs for family-size units, while others raised neighborhood parking problems.
6 Blane Street pole: Residents asked that the pole be moved away from the house, and petitioners agreed to move it 20 feet, to 30 feet south of pole 2023.
Broadway and Eastern conduit: Members said the underground work must be reviewed against the Broadway redesign, so the item was split off for a new petition.
